clue.text: Presenter's screen captures hit from the east

indicators.note: the screen word holds the other piece inside it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: a door screens a room off, so it can stand for one

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, so the hit word runs backwards

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat or hit them

explanation.surface: A TV host's screen is showing footage of a blow seen coming from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns TAN into NAT, which 'captures' puts inside DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A donator gives or presents something, so the giver is a presenter of a gift.

clue.text: Damper device — put in pocket

parts.note: to dash is to throw or hurl, as a shot is put
to pot a ball in snooker is to pocket it

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip a small damping gadget into one's pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashpot is a mechanical shock absorber that slows motion through fluid resistance, as on a door closer.

clue.text: Wrong thing for arousal, take right off!

definitions.text: Wrong thing for arousal, take right off!

indicators.note: arousal means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
with 'off' after it, to take something off is to remove it from the word before

explanation.surface: Advice that a modest garment is no good for passion, so remove it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... right off' removes R from WRONG to leave WONG; 'for arousal' stirs WONG and THING together. The whole clue also describes a dowdy garment that kills desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, loose bedtime garment is hardly seductive wear, hence the wrong outfit for passion.

clue.text: Satellite station broadcast fading so

indicators.note: scattered like seed, so the station's letters are thrown into a new order
the word so fades away, its letters dropping out of the station word first

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio station's signal is weakening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fading so' removes S and O from STATION, leaving TATIN, which 'broadcast' scatters into the moon's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Publicity in European capital for aerial protector

indicators.note: the publicity word sits inside the capital city's name

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: An advertising campaign in a European city promotes a guard for an antenna.
explanation.definitionFit: A radome is a dome-shaped weatherproof housing that shields a radar antenna.

clue.text: Joke about priest almost in container

indicators.note: the joke word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the priest word is dropped

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader, loosely a priest

explanation.surface: A joke about a clergyman is mostly inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RABBI to RABB, and 'about' puts GAG round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grab bag is a bag or box of assorted items to dip into, so a kind of container.

clue.text: Nan's left with form of epilepsy

parts.note: Nan is an informal name for a grandmother; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Granny has been left with a type of epilepsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "Nan's" reads as 'has', joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand mal is the old name for a generalised tonic-clonic seizure, a severe type of epileptic attack.

clue.text: Painting I suppress is something often associated with Jerusalem

parts.note: painting is a form of art
to choke back is to suppress

explanation.surface: An artist confesses to hiding a picture linked to the Holy City.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerusalem here is not the city: the Jerusalem artichoke is a knobbly root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is a well-known tuber that carries the city's name in its own.

clue.text: English philosopher without transport back

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: no means without, as in 'no money' for without money
a cab is a means of transport

explanation.surface: An English thinker is left stranded with no way to get home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NOCAB into the philosopher's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and statesman, a pioneer of scientific method.

clue.text: Opal, for instance seen on ring held by young woman

indicators.note: the young woman's letters hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: a girl is a young woman

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: as means for instance, as in 'cities such as Paris'
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An opal set on a ring is worn by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Girasol is a fire opal that shows a shifting glow, a variety of the gem.

clue.text: Referred to as heard and seen

indicators.note: as heard tells us the word is spoken aloud, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: something referred to is cited

explanation.surface: Something mentioned by ear and also spotted by eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sighted has been spotted, so it is visible to an observer.

clue.text: One found out and about on river vehicle

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: to found is to cast metal, so the following word is recast into new letters

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone discovered out and about by the river with a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocar is an old term for a motor car, a self-propelled road vehicle.

clue.text: Impatience tends to ruin remedies not needing prescription

indicators.note: ruin means wreck, so the letters of the two words are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Impatient people are inclined to spoil over-the-counter cures.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent medicines are proprietary remedies sold freely over the counter, without a doctor's prescription.

clue.text: Hospital ignored during a long depression

indicators.note: the hospital letter is left out of the word for during

parts.note: through means during, as in 'through the night'

explanation.surface: A patient endured a long low spell while the hospital ignored them.
explanation.walkthrough: THROUGH loses one H; 'a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long narrow hollow, in land, weather charts or economic cycles.

clue.text: Make more desirable? I'm so large unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately signals that things have gone wrong, here the letters' order

explanation.surface: Someone overweight wonders how to improve their image.
explanation.definitionFit: To glamorise something is to make it look more attractive than it is.

clue.text: Musical start in us state

indicators.note: the start word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
to rouse is to start, as one starts or rouses game from cover

explanation.surface: A show opens in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical, so this names a show.

clue.text: A softened composition? No good for one such

definitions.text: A softened composition? No good for one such

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are composed afresh

explanation.surface: A gentle piece of music is wasted on someone who cannot hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is signalled by 'composition'; the rest of the clue says a piece of music, however soft, is useless to such a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone totally unable to hear gets nothing from any piece of music.

clue.text: Chambers has it as "most mad"

parts.note: Chambers is the dictionary setters use, which lists this word as craziest; chambers are also chamber pots, which the word's first part echoes

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry gives a superlative of madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers wants to be read as rooms or pots; it is the dictionary, which gives this informal superlative of potty, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty is informal British for crazy, and its superlative means the craziest of all.

clue.text: Writer needs identification in military HQ

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tag is a label giving identification
in and on can both mean happening or in progress, as in 'the game is on'

explanation.surface: An author needs an ID card to get into army headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense in Virginia.

clue.text: No stamp? That could trouble me

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A letter carrier worries about an unstamped envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the definition: the clue is spoken by the person who delivers the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The speaker is the mail carrier, the one bothered by a letter without postage.

clue.text: Birds seen around river with duck?

definitions.text: Birds seen around river with duck?

indicators.note: the birds word goes around the other letters

parts.note: hens are birds
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Wading birds spotted near water alongside ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: these wading birds are typically seen by rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: These tall grey wading birds hunt fish along riverbanks, often among the ducks.

clue.text: Games of tennis just when the weather's good

parts.note: a set is a group of games in tennis
just means fair, as in a just ruling

explanation.surface: Tennis matches are played only when the sun is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer's 'set fair' reading forecasts settled, fine conditions.

clue.text: With which some can become so entangled

parts.words: With which some can become so
parts.note: the answer, split in two, is an instruction: the word some loses its first pronoun and becomes so

explanation.surface: A net in which some creatures get caught up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after two letters: shed the pronoun M-E from SOME and SO is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Meshed means caught up or interlocked, as in a net.

clue.text: Premiership team's current best player is impulsive

definitions.meaning: read whimsically: a Spur is a Tottenham Hotspur footballer, and this is their man in form right now
acting on a sudden whim, without thought

explanation.surface: A football club's star man is reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur, known as Spurs, is a London club in the English Premier League.
explanation.definitionFit: An unplanned, spontaneous act is done without forethought, hence impulsive; the first reading is a footballer's award.

clue.text: Fruit put back in in utensil? Guess!

indicators.note: put back means the run of letters is turned to read in reverse
in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A guessing game about fruit placed back in a kitchen tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is the hidden-word signal; inside 'utensil? Guess' sits SILGU, which 'put back' turns round. Uglis are Jamaican citrus fruits.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Moderate ignoring sun many times

indicators.note: the sun letter is left out of the moderate word

parts.note: to soften is to moderate

explanation.surface: Tone things down without regard for the sun, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, happening on many occasions.

clue.text: One is gripped by man flu perhaps

indicators.note: the man word grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: a male is a man
one is A, the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man suffering with the famously exaggerated man flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man flu' is a jokey phrase for a cold that men supposedly overdramatise.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu brings on a general feeling of being unwell, an example of that vague sickness.

clue.text: Old pro is rubbished in the area

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A former prostitute is dismissed in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a hetaera was a high-class courtesan, so a working girl of old.

clue.text: New climb starting to develop

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A fresh route up the mountain is beginning to take shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, in its earliest stage.

clue.text: A couple of fellows without energy, in other words finished

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the fellows go round the energy letter

parts.note: two words for fellow: a don is a university fellow, and F abbreviates fellow
two words for fellow: a don is a university fellow, and F abbreviates fellow
E is the physics symbol for energy
or introduces an alternative, as in other words does

explanation.surface: Two academics, out of steam, are in other words exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside puts DON and F round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done for is to be ruined or beaten, beyond saving.
